prompt:
**(a)** Classify each function as odd, even or neither: $f(x)=x^{3}-x$, $g(x)=x^{2}\cos x$, $h(x)=x^{2}+x$. **[3]**

**(b)** Describe the symmetry of the graph of an odd function. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $f(-x)=-x^{3}+x=-f(x)$: odd **(A1)**; $g(-x)=x^{2}\cos x=g(x)$: even **(A1)**; $h(-x)=x^{2}-x$, which is neither $h(x)$ nor $-h(x)$: neither **(A1)**

**(b)** Rotational symmetry of order 2 about the origin **(A1)** (an even function is symmetric in the $y$-axis).

prompt:
Let $f(x)=(x-2)^{2}+1$.

**(a)** Explain why $f$ has no inverse for $x\in\mathbb{R}$. **[1]**

**(b)** State the largest domain of the form $x\ge k$ for which $f^{-1}$ exists. **[1]**

**(c)** For this domain, find $f^{-1}(x)$ and its domain. **[3]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $f$ is not one-to-one, e.g. $f(1)=f(3)=2$ **(R1)**

**(b)** $x\ge2$ (to the right of the vertex) **(A1)**

**(c)** $y-1=(x-2)^{2}\Rightarrow x=2+\sqrt{y-1}$ (positive root because $x\ge2$) **(M1)(A1)**; $f^{-1}(x)=2+\sqrt{x-1}$, $x\ge1$ **(A1)**

prompt: Show that $f(x)=\dfrac{3x+1}{x-3}$, $x\neq3$, is self-inverse, and state a geometric property of its graph.
markscheme:
$y=\dfrac{3x+1}{x-3}\Rightarrow yx-3y=3x+1\Rightarrow x(y-3)=3y+1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3y+1}{y-3}$ **(M1)**

So $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{3x+1}{x-3}=f(x)$ **(A1)**

The graph is symmetric in the line $y=x$ **(A1)**
